On Finishing Things Badly

There is a version of on finishing things badly that gets discussed in grand terms — frameworks, rules, a complete reset. Most of it is noise. What lasts is usually one unglamorous choice made on a day nobody was watching.

That is the part worth paying attention to. Not the plan, but the small input you would still repeat if no one saw the result. It is slower than a promise and far more reliable than a burst of effort.

Which small input in your own routine would still be there if nobody noticed?

#TheNineStitches

slides.caption: Everyone talks about on finishing things badly. Nobody talks about this.
We optimize for the wrong thing and call it discipline.
Depth needs time, silence, and the luxury of boredom.
Pick one thing today and let the rest wait.
Pick one input and start this week.
